Edito CMS is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). Due to improper input validation, an authenticated attacker can inject malicious scripts into givenName and surname parameters via the /api/auth/profile endpoint. When an administrator visits the admin changelog logs, the injected script is automatically executed, in his browser. This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607. Edito CMS is vulnerable to Dynamic LINQ injection. Due to improper input validation, an authenticated attacker can inject conditional expressions into the sort parameter of paginated administrative endpoints. Analyzing the returned result order allows the attacker to extract value of any field character by character, leading to potential exposure of sensitive data. This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607. Edito CMS is vulnerable to improper cryptographic signature verification in the JWT refresh logic. An authenticated low-privilege user can submit self-crafted​ ​JWT​ containing​ ​an existing user​ ​identifier and, due to the lack of signature validation,​​ obtain​ ​a ​​valid,​​ fully-signed​​ session ​​token​​ for​​ any ​​account ​​in​ ​the​ ​system. This allows the attacker to impersonate any user, including administrators. This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607. The MISP Modules website component contains an open redirect vulnerability in its login endpoint. The /login route accepted a user-supplied next query parameter and passed it directly to Flask's redirect() function without validating the destination. An attacker could craft a URL such as https://victim-host/login?next=https://attacker.example/phish and deliver it to a user (e.g., via email or a lookalike page). After the user successfully authenticated, the application issued a 302 redirect to the attacker-controlled external URL. This enables phishing attacks where a user, believing they are still on the legitimate MISP Modules site, may enter additional credentials or sensitive information on the attacker's page. It can also be used to obscure the true destination of a link, bypassing user trust in the legitimate domain. The vulnerability requires the victim to interact with the crafted URL and complete a login, but no prior authentication or special configuration is needed on the attacker's side. The affected component is the website sub-project of misp-modules, specifically the account blueprint in website/app/account/account.py.
